The world's newest languages
The connection between language and gender
Why mothers are better language teachers

A BBC presenter

questions.q: How does Professor Boroditsky explain the phrase 'mother tongue'?
options: Women have always spoken more than men in families
Mothers usually looked after us and taught us things
It was first used in an old poem about childhood
It only exists in English and a few related languages
questions.why: She links it to mothers as primary caregivers and people who teach us things.

questions.q: What does Professor Boroditsky say about other languages?
options: They all use exactly the same phrase as English does
None of them have any gendered words for language
They differ, but many use a similar metaphor
They use 'father tongue' instead of 'mother tongue'
questions.why: She says different languages do it differently, but the metaphor applies in a lot of languages.

questions.q: Which pairs of words does Professor Boroditsky give as examples of gendered words?
options: Actor and actress, waiter and waitress
King and queen, prince and princess
Father and mother, son and daughter
Host and hostess, hero and heroine

questions.q: According to Professor Boroditsky, how do people often see the masculine form of a job?
options: As less skilled
As more old-fashioned
As exactly the same
As more important and skilled
questions.why: People perceive the masculine form as a more prestigious or more skilled job.

questions.q: What problem can these different attitudes lead to?
options: Fewer people learning languages
Differences in pay
People changing their names
Confusion about spelling
questions.why: She says they 'could then come with pay disparities'.
